description: No complete enumerated list yet of Hungarian state-owned or state-controlled financial-sector contracting authorities (beyond MNB, Magyar Államkincstár, Magyar Posta, Diákhitel Központ, MÁV) whose own disclosure pages should be monitored.

The exact CPV code set for banking/payment technology in HU procurement is not yet fixed. Only CPV 30144200 (jegykiadó gépek) was confirmed by name; codes for ATMs, cash-handling, card personalisation and self-service kiosks remain to be pinned down.
Vendor names in HU notices appear in inconsistent legal forms (Zrt./Kft./Nyrt., accented vs unaccented, Hungarian subsidiary vs group brand), which will fragment award counts.
Framework-agreement call-offs under the KEF centralised system may not generate individual public award notices, hiding the actual vendor-buyer pair for central-government payment/IT purchases.

No confirmed Hungarian term set yet for 'card personalisation' and 'self-service banking kiosk' as they are actually written in procurement notices; the seed term 'kártyaszemélyesítés' returned no procurement hits.
Historical depth is unassessed: EKR only became mandatory from 2018, so pre-2018 awards live in older Értesítő archives with a different structure.
The mapping from banking/payments subject matter to actual CPV codes used by Hungarian buyers has not been empirically validated — it is currently an assumption.

TED and EU-funded award databases cover public buyers. Commercial Hungarian banks (OTP, K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, MBH, UniCredit, CIB) procure payments technology privately and appear only when state-owned or EU-cofunded.
Hungarian supplier names in TED/EKR appear with varying legal-form suffixes (Kft., Zrt., Nyrt., Bt.), accents and consortium constructions; no normalisation or tax-number join has been designed.

Much Hungarian public IT buying runs through central purchasing bodies and framework agreements (központosított közbeszerzés, keretmegállapodás), where the TED award names the framework holder and the real call-offs are invisible.
Hungarian national portals migrate content (archive.palyazat.gov.hu already exists as a separate archive host), so links captured today may move.

Job ads are the most perishable source class in this run: HU board ads typically expire in 30-60 days and are then removed from both the board and the search index, so any signal not captured within the window is lost permanently.
The two highest-yield sources for vendor-side signals (LinkedIn Jobs, Glassdoor) are auth-walled and ToS-restricted, so they cannot be part of an automated pipeline.

Employer watchlist currently covers large banks, GIRO, MNB and a few HU software firms. Missing: UniCredit HU, CIB, Gránit, MagNet, MBH Fintechlab, Takarék entities, MFB, plus HU-based card processors, ATM independent deployers (Euronet HU), acquirers and PSPs, and the bank IT captives (e.g. Deutsche Telekom/IT Services Hungary, Diebold/NCR service partners).

A stable HU keyword set for banking/payments job ads is only partially established (core banki rendszer, rendszerszervező, integrációs fejlesztő, POS terminál, ATM üzemeltetés, pénzforgalom, kártyarendszer, azonnali fizetés/AFR, qvik). Noisy terms not yet flagged: 'bank' matches non-financial employers, 'terminál' matches logistics, 'core' matches unrelated English-in-HU usage.
No baseline exists for normal hiring volume per employer, so a spike (the actual weak signal) cannot yet be distinguished from routine churn or seasonal recruitment.
No source yet covering ATM / cash logistics / branch self-service events and their exhibitor lists in Hungary.
Only one trade-fair exhibitor directory (Sirha Budapest) captured. Retail-technology and merchant-facing fairs where POS/payment acceptance vendors exhibit are otherwise unmapped.
Sponsor rosters were confirmed only for recent editions; the multi-year time series that would show vendor entry, exit and tier escalation has not been assembled.

International award programmes that rank Hungarian banks (Global Finance, Euromoney, The Banker country awards, Mastercard/Visa regional awards) were not searched, though they are frequently cited by Hungarian banks in their own PR.

The highest-value signal in this cell — a bank executive and a named supplier co-presenting a case study — requires parsing speaker affiliation pairs per session, which no source publishes in structured form.
Foreign branches (fióktelep) and cross-border service providers were not systematically explored; a foreign payments vendor may serve HU banks with no Hungarian Kft. at all.
No TEÁOR/NACE-code-driven screen of the full HU supplier population was executed — only name-based lookups of known vendors.
Other Hungarian credit/company-information houses (e.g. Crefoport, Coface Hungary, Creditreform, EMIS/CEIC-type regional databases) were not searched in this pass.
Historical ownership change tracking (who bought which HU vendor, when) was identified conceptually via cégtörténet and Cégközlöny archives, but no archive depth/retention limits were established.

English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature — the statutory portals and filings are Hungarian-only, and English guides found were mostly commercial company-formation marketing of low evidential value.
Healthcare buyers (hospitals, clinics, ÁEEK/OKFŐ-managed institutions) are entirely uncovered for kiosks, patient check-in terminals and payment automats.
Utilities (MVM Next, regional víziközmű and távhő providers) and their customer-service payment points are not represented among the sources.

EU-level procurement (TED - Tenders Electronic Daily) was not searched, although the largest HU automat/kiosk contracts are above threshold and are published there in both hu and en with structured CPV data.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only vendor-global material (NCR/Diebold Nixdorf corporate) surfaced, with no en-language HU market analysis.
Supplier attribution for private retail chains is missing across the board; sources give installed base but not who supplied it.
Cash-handling specifics (cash recycling, CIT, smart safes) for retail and fuel buyers are not represented; only card and ticketing evidence was found.
Támogatásokat Vizsgáló Iroda (TVI, the Hungarian state aid monitoring office at the Ministry of Finance) and any national de minimis / aid register were not searched in this pass.

EU centrally-managed programmes that also fund financial/payment digitalisation in Hungary were out of the searched set: Digital Europe Programme, Horizon Europe, InvestEU / EIF guarantee intermediaries, and Interreg. Their beneficiary databases (CORDIS, Funding & Tenders portal, EIF intermediary lists) name Hungarian fintech and IT participants.
Kohesio's Hungarian coverage for the 2021-2027 period is described as progressively backfilled; the actual completeness for GINOP Plusz / DIMOP Plusz records was not verified.

No verified crosswalk was established between grant project codes (e.g. DIMOP_Plusz-1.3.7-23-2023-00001) and company identifiers (adószám / cégjegyzékszám), which is needed to link beneficiaries to company registry and financial data.
Regional OPs (TOP Plusz) and county-level grant decisions that fund municipal digital service and e-payment projects were only glimpsed via one filtered URL and not systematically explored.

All candidates were identified from search-result metadata and article summaries; individual pages were not fetched, so paywall depth, robots.txt posture and archive completeness are unassessed. Finextra, PYMNTS and Statista are known to deploy bot defences that may return 403 to naive crawlers.

Several plausible international outlets in this cell were not reached in the searches performed: Electronic Payments International, The Banker, Central Banking, Nilson Report, Merchant Payments Ecosystem / PaymentsCMI, ATM Marketplace, Payments Dive, Sifted, and the S&P Global / Fitch / Moody's Hungarian bank sector commentary.

Search-driven discovery in this cell skews to OTP Bank and Erste Bank Hungary. The merged MBH Bank (MKB + Budapest Bank + Takarékbank), K&H (KBC), CIB (Intesa), Raiffeisen Hungary, Gránit Bank, and domestic acquirers/PSPs (Barion, B-Payment Szolgáltató Zrt., SRS Informatika Kft., Cellum, OTP Mobil/Simple, QVIK) were barely represented.

Retrievable items skew recent or to a few landmark deals (2014 OTPay, 2018-2019 instant payments, 2023 iGCB core banking, 2025-2026 items). Whether these outlets' archives are fully open and searchable back a decade is unknown.

The highest-value assets in this cell (GlobalData Hungary Cards and Payments to 2030, Euromonitor Financial Cards and Payments in Hungary, IBSi Sales League Table, Mordor Hungary POS Terminal) are all licensed products; no procurement decision or price discovery was made.
The exact fields exposed per institution in Intézménykereső (licence type, licence date, agents, passporting, ownership) were not enumerated — only the register's existence was confirmed.
MNB maintains an /en/ mirror, but it is unclear whether the payment statistics table sets, Aranykönyv and the Payment Systems Report are fully translated or only partially.

This cell covers MNB only; the infrastructure operator GIRO Zrt. (giro.hu) and KELER are named by MNB but are separate publishers with their own participant lists and technical documentation, and were not scouted here.
The decisions search was identified but its filtering parameters, result export options and coverage depth (how far back, whether PDFs are downloadable) were not tested.

qvik (the MNB-backed QR/deeplink instant payment brand) appears in the newest statistics releases but I did not locate an MNB-published list of qvik-accepting PSPs, merchants or technical service providers.

Erste, UniCredit and CIB are subsidiaries of foreign groups (Erste Group, UniCredit S.p.A., Intesa Sanpaolo); group-level press rooms and annual reports were not scouted in this cell and may carry the Hungary-relevant technology decisions.
Most bank press rooms were located but their historical pagination depth and any RSS/JSON feeds were not established; only CIB showed an explicit year-archive pattern and MBH a date-slug pattern.
Pillar 3 / nyilvánosságra hozatal disclosures and ICT/outsourcing registers under DORA were not systematically located per bank; only OTP's 'Nyilvánosságra hozatal' page surfaced.
The statutory e-beszámoló filing portal (company annual accounts) was not reached in this pass, though third-party registries (OPTEN, Nemzeti Cégtár) appeared as pointers.

Bank-owned non-web channels — LinkedIn company pages, YouTube channels, developer/API portals and careers pages — were not scouted; job ads and API docs are among the most reliable indirect reveals of the technology stack in use.
VIBER (the MNB-operated RTGS) was identified as an in-scope infrastructure but not separately source-mapped in this pass; its technology supply chain is distinct from GIRO's.
PCI SSC's approved-vendor programmes (Card Production & Provisioning Security, P2PE, PIN Security, approved PTS devices) were reasoned as relevant but not yet enumerated as concrete sources.
Mastercard Europe Kft. and Visa's Hungarian legal entities were not mapped in the company register during this pass (headcount, officers, local footprint).
GIRO's supplier-contract PDF is a point-in-time snapshot (a 2025-08-31 version was surfaced); prior versions may not remain online.
Card personalisation searching in Hungarian returned mostly generic plastic-card printers; scheme-certified EMV personalisation is discussed almost entirely in English or not at all publicly.

Bank-side acquirers other than OTP and Erste were not covered in this pass: MBH Bank, K&H (beyond one qvik PDF), Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB and Gránit — all of which either acquire directly or resell a PSP's terminal estate.

Independent/softPOS and terminal-adjacent challengers were only touched via secondary coverage (Billingo x Global Payments softPOS). SumUp, myPOS, Viva.com, Revolut Reader and local ISO/distributors were not systematically searched.

No procurement/tender source was inspected. Public-sector acquiring and terminal contracts (Magyar Posta, Magyar Államkincstár, NÚSZ — all named as SimplePay partners) are typically awarded via published tenders.
Case-study material is thin: no vendor case-study libraries, conference agendas or award submissions were captured beyond the OTP Mobil partner awards article and EkerNap.
Several anchor facts found are historical (Global Payments/Erste 2014, Worldline-SIX 2018, GVH inquiry 2019); 2025-2026 partnership flow was captured mostly for Revolut and qvik.
English-language investor/analyst material on Nexi, Worldline and Global Payments was only lightly sampled; group-level results decks often break out CEE/Hungary volumes.
No sources found for Ingenico, Verifone or PAX naming Hungarian customers; the POS-terminal supplier map for HU is effectively empty from this cell.
No Hungarian-language vendor case-study corpus exists for the international vendors in this cell; the hu-language evidence base is limited to local integrators and trade press.

Several vendor case-study libraries are PDF-only or behind registration forms (Diebold Nixdorf media files, ATM Marketplace resources, Thales resource downloads), so the presence or absence of a Hungarian client could not be settled by search alone.

The strongest confirmed HU vendor evidence clusters in 1997-2020 (Euronet-Budapest Bank, ACI-OTP/Erste/Takarekinfo). Recent 2023-2026 supplier changes — including the MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék merger into MBH Bank and the reported Brink's acquisition of NCR Atleos — are not yet reflected.

Snowballing surfaced non-listed vendors relevant to HU (valantic at Erste Bank Hungary; Capsys and T-Systems Magyarország as ACI delivery partners), showing the eleven-vendor cell definition understates the actual HU supplier landscape.

Several likely local competitors were not yet investigated: Synergon, WSH (rendszerintegracio), Online Üzleti Informatika Zrt., Scriptum, ITSH/Deutsche Telekom Systems Hungary, Nexon, and the Hungarian arms of Accenture/Deloitte that act as bank-side prime consultants.
No job-advertisement source was captured. Hungarian job boards (profession.hu, LinkedIn HU) are a strong indirect signal: integrator postings routinely name the client bank's platform and project.
MNB-side sources on bank IT outsourcing (kiszervezési nyilvántartás / outsourcing registers, supervisory inspection reports naming IT suppliers) were not searched in this pass.
English-language coverage of the local integrator set is thin — most of these firms publish substantive references only in Hungarian, and only the foreign-vendor announcements were found in English.
Only current-state pages were identified; historical reference lists that vendors have since removed were not sought.
Portfolio.hu (Signature), vg.hu and Forbes.hu place a meaningful portion of their deepest bank-technology reporting behind paywalls; free crawling captures headline and lede only.
Historical bank-IT deal reporting (pre-2015) on Bitport, HWSW and possibly Computerworld.hu was not systematically enumerated in this pass; only individual old articles surfaced opportunistically.

The bank-side actor map is incomplete: coverage clustered on OTP, MBH (ex-Magyar Bankholding / MKB / Budapest Bank / Takarék) and a few challengers; K&H, Erste, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, CIB, Gránit, MagNet, Cofidis and the Posta/Kincstár channel were barely represented.

English-language coverage of Hungarian bank IT deals was thin in this pass; only international vendor announcements (e.g. Thought Machine) appear to cross over, and mostly via Hungarian outlets first.

Payments-specific and card/acquiring-specific Hungarian trade coverage (AFR/instant payments scheme participants, POS acquiring, card personalisation) was only touched incidentally; no dedicated payments trade outlet was identified for HU.

All URLs in this slice are proposed from search results and article listings; none were confirmed reachable by this agent, and several (BankTechShow event site, Bankár Magazin) were surfaced only at domain level.

Savings-cooperative / integrated-cooperative and regional-bank representation bodies were not separately located in this pass; after the MBH consolidation it is unclear whether a distinct takarékszövetkezeti interest body still maintains a public member roster.

Association CONFERENCE and EVENT sponsor/exhibitor lists were not systematically harvested. Bankszövetség, IVSZ, HFA (Budapest Fintech Week) and Ecommerce Hungary all run events whose sponsor tiers reveal which vendors are actively spending to reach Hungarian banks — often the fastest signal of a new market entrant.

Case studies are the weakest topic in this cell. Association directories enumerate WHO exists but rarely document WHAT was implemented at which bank; only Bankszövetség publications and NJSZT/IVSZ conference material hint at implementation detail.
Most rosters in this cell exist only in Hungarian; English versions (Bankszövetség /en/, HFA's English Fintech Report) are abridged and lag the Hungarian pages.

EU-funded cluster/EDIH consortium rosters (e.g. DigitalTech EDIH, of which Blockchain Hungary is a consortium member) and the Blockchain Koalíció founder list were identified only indirectly and not enumerated.
